A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Atom Theory work. The main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C are readable and can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original representation-shift analyses, TSAE training experiments, atom evaluations and monosemanticity results in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: V3 retains the original empirical results and additionally reports a ReLU SAE capacity control in Table 6 and further GPT-J layer-level results.

M1.justification: The AIP formulation, TSAE architecture, threshold activation, identification procedure and reconstruction–sparsity objective remain unchanged. The new normalization note describes a remedy for excluded layers without establishing a revision to the method used for the retained results.

E1.justification: Documented coverage retains WikiData/CounterFact, Wikipedia and MATH500. GPT-J was already evaluated in v2. Section 6 mentions preliminary diffusion-model observations but supplies no specified additional task or evaluation.

E2.justification: Neurons, GemmaScope and LlamaScope features, and standard ReLU SAEs remain the evaluated comparators. ReLU SAEs already appear in v2 Table 3; v3 Table 6 varies their capacity without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: V3 adds a controlled capacity sweep using 4×, 5×, 6× and 7× ReLU SAEs at Gemma2-2B layer 10 (Table 6). This introduces limited additional experimental configurations; the retained experiments' datasets, metrics and stated settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new ReLU capacity control tests whether increasing capacity remedies the previously observed limitations. Appendix C.3 also adds failure analysis reporting that normalization and reparameterization largely resolve optimization problems in Llama3.1-8B layers 30–31.

E5.justification: Both versions report monosemanticity means and standard errors using ten sampled units per selected layer (Appendix C.7). No changes to seeds, repeated-run reporting, uncertainty estimation or significance testing are reported.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports ReLU R2 values of 0.9183, 0.9173, 0.9150 and 0.9143 at capacities 4×–7×, with q* values of 0.4768, 0.4655, 0.4514 and 0.4532. V3 also adds GPT-J layer-level distributions and a qualitative normalization outcome. Tables 1–5 and the original plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorem statements and Appendix A proofs are unchanged, as are the Appendix C metric definitions. The added gauge-symmetry discussion provides conceptual interpretation without a new formal result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: Atom Theory, AIP-based geometry, faithfulness/stability criteria, TSAE identifiability and empirical identification of near-ideal atoms. Wording refinements do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: New Section 6 substantially expands interpretation through applicability arguments beyond LLMs, a functional-equivalence interpretation of near-ideal Pareto solutions, and discussion of finite-capacity corpus training and downstream applications. Appendix C.3 additionally attributes the Llama optimization failures primarily to unusually high data variance.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly describes dividing training data by its distributional standard deviation and reparameterizing the trained model to address the Llama failures. Those layers remain excluded from reported scores. Existing hyperparameters, hardware costs and code access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds references supporting RIP, coherence and sparse recovery. Section 5 adds positioning relative to attention heads, circuits, localized components and compressed-sensing approaches, while retaining the principal neurons-versus-features framing.

P1.justification: V3 inserts a Discussion section before the retained conclusion, adds introductory section pointers and an explanation of the radar plots, and makes localized wording corrections. Acknowledgements, correspondence details and publication information are added; most existing prose and organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds GPT-J Figures 9 and 25 and the capacity-control Table 6. Existing displays are retained but renumbered and regrouped across appendix pages. The judge prompt is newly boxed, although it becomes split across pages 37 and 40.

improvement.justification: The ReLU capacity control adds useful evidence about an alternative explanation for the baseline's limitations, and the additional GPT-J plots and normalization guidance improve empirical documentation. These gains are limited: the principal results and proofs remain unchanged, broader applicability remains speculative, and the excluded Llama layers still lack reported scores.
